findings.finding: The load-bearing claim that Claude's `can_use_tool` callback IS the Action-Gateway mutation chokepoint (RESEARCH R-CC headline, ADR-006, ARCH §4.2 Law #1) does NOT hold for all mutation paths. Per the official Agent SDK permission-evaluation flow, `canUseTool` is the LAST resort step, reached only if not resolved by hooks/deny-rules/permission-mode/allow-rules. Concretely: (a) subagents spawned by the Task tool INHERIT the parent's permission mode and it 'cannot be overridden per subagent' — if the parent ever runs in `bypassPermissions`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`, subagent tool calls (incl. their Bash/Write/Edit mutations) execute with NO approval prompt and NEVER hit `canUseTool`; (b) confirmed OPEN bug claude-code#27203: in `default` mode, BACKGROUND subagent (Task `run_in_background:true`) tool calls are denied INTERNALLY without invoking `canUseTool`, and this corrupts the parent session transport ('Stream closed'); (c) `acceptEdits` mode auto-approves file edits AND filesystem commands (`mkdir`,`rm`,`mv`,`cp`,`sed`) without `canUseTool`. NexusOps's entire 'single mutation chokepoint' invariant depends on EVERY agent mutation funnelling through `can_use_tool` -> Gateway; subagent/background-bash/non-default-mode paths are holes. RESEARCH.md tagged R-CC entirely VERIFIED and never tested the coverage of `can_use_tool` across subagents/MCP/background-bash — exactly the verification this dimension was asked to check. This is the single most load-bearing unverified dep in the plan.
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions: permission order = Hooks -> Deny rules -> Permission mode (bypassPermissions/acceptEdits approve here) -> Allow rules -> canUseTool ('If not resolved by any of the above'). 'Subagent inheritance: When the parent uses bypassPermissions, acceptEdits, or auto, all subagents inherit that mode and it cannot be overridden per subagent ... grants them full, autonomous system access without any approval prompts.' acceptEdits auto-approves Edit/Write + mkdir/rm/mv/cp/sed. GitHub anthropics/claude-code#27203 (OPEN): 'canUseTool callback not invoked for background subagent tool calls in default permission mode' — SDK denies internally without invoking the callback and corrupts the parent transport ('Stream closed'). RESEARCH.md L59 calls can_use_tool 'literally the Action-Gateway mutation chokepoint inside the harness [VERIFIED]' with no coverage caveat; ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4.2 Law #1 lists 'can_use_tool' as the agent feed into the sole chokepoint.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Harness Adapter Layer (Claude model) + §Action Gateway (defense-in-depth): (1) Promote a NEW pre-build spike OQ-HARN-SPIKE-7 'can_use_tool mutation-path coverage' that empirically maps which tool calls reach the callback vs bypass it for: direct Bash/Write/Edit, MCP server tools (mcp__*), Task-tool subagents (foreground and background), and each permission mode. (2) State as a LOCKED invariant that NexusOps-driven Claude sessions run ONLY in `default` permission mode (never acceptEdits/bypassPermissions/auto) so subagents cannot inherit a bypass; document this as a hard constraint, not a default. (3) Add defense-in-depth so the Gateway is not solely dependent on can_use_tool: combine `PreToolUse` hooks (which the docs show run FIRST, before mode/allow rules) as a redundant interception layer, plus deny-rule lockdown of dangerous Bash patterns, and treat the can_use_tool callback as one of several layers. (4) Until #27203 is fixed, FORBID background subagents (Task run_in_background) in supervised sessions, or pin a Claude version where coverage is verified. Bind these to RISK PR-02/TR-09 and the §4.2 'single chokepoint' law.

findings.finding: The 2026-06-15 Agent-SDK separate credit pool is materially UNDER-assessed. RESEARCH.md L65 records it correctly as VERIFIED but reduces the consequence to 'surface in cost projections', and the architecture only echoes this in PR-06 ('surface CC Agent-SDK credit-pool split'). The real, now-confirmed impact is structural: from 2026-06-15 (8 days out), ALL Claude Agent SDK / `claude -p` usage on subscription plans draws from a SEPARATE, CAPPED monthly credit pool ($20 Pro / $100 Max5x / $200 Max20x) billed at API list rates, with NO rollover and NO automatic fallback — 'once that credit runs out, automated requests stop entirely.' NexusOps's primary Claude adapter (ADR-006) is built on SDK streaming-input + can_use_tool, so EVERY supervised Claude session — including the PRD §25 demo itself — consumes this finite pool. A Pro user ($20) supervising agents could exhaust it in hours, after which the cockpit's core supervision path silently stops. This is not a cost-display issue; it is a viability constraint on the load-bearing SDK-driven design and on the demo. Interactive Claude Code in the terminal is explicitly UNAFFECTED — which means the PTY-driven path (currently the ADR-006 'fallback') may be the only sustainable mode for cost-sensitive users, inverting the primary/fallback relationship.
findings.evidence: Multiple 2026-06 sources (techtimes, thenewstack 'Anthropic Agent SDK gets separate credit pools', startdebugging, support.claude.com art.15036540): effective 2026-06-15, Agent SDK + `claude -p` + Claude Code GitHub Actions + 3rd-party apps via Agent SDK move to a separate monthly dollar credit ($20/$100/$200 by plan), API list pricing, no rollover, hard stop on exhaustion, no auto-fallback; interactive chat / terminal Claude Code unaffected. RESEARCH.md L65 footnotes it ('surface in cost projections'); DRAFT §9.1 and ADR-006 make SDK streaming-input the PRIMARY Claude path with PTY+hooks only as a FALLBACK; PR-06 mentions only 'surface the credit-pool split'.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Harness Adapter Layer (Claude model) + §Execution Profiles + §Usage/Cost Projection: (1) Add a RISK row (e.g. TR-14 'Agent-SDK credit-pool exhaustion halts SDK-driven supervision') with the hard-stop/no-fallback behavior called out. (2) Reconsider ADR-006's primary/fallback ordering: state explicitly whether the MVP default is SDK-driven (pays into the pool) or interactive-PTY-driven (interactive subscription, no pool draw) and the criteria for switching — this is a load-bearing human decision, not a footnote. (3) The usage projection MUST track Agent-SDK-pool consumption per execution profile and surface 'pool remaining / will-stop-when-exhausted' so the cockpit warns BEFORE supervision silently dies, including during the demo. (4) Verify the demo (PRD §25) does not assume free SDK usage on the build account.

findings.finding: RESEARCH.md never verified that the Claude adapter's mutation interception covers MCP-server tools (mcp__<server>__<tool>) — only direct built-in tools were considered. NexusOps itself, cc-crew, CodeGraph and Context7 all expose capabilities as MCP tools, and agents under supervision will call them. Per the SDK docs, MCP tools 'fall through to permission_mode and can_use_tool' the same as built-ins, which is reassuring for DIRECT calls — but the same subagent-inheritance and #27203 background-subagent gaps apply to MCP tool calls too, and an MCP tool that itself mutates (e.g. a cc-crew or git MCP) would do so inside the harness, outside the Gateway's resource model. The draft's Law #1 lists 'Brain (MCP tool proposals)' as feeding the Gateway, but does not address agent-invoked MCP tools from OTHER servers, which are not Gateway intents.
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions + /mcp: 'allowed_tools ... a tool not listed ... falls through to permission mode and canUseTool'; tool naming mcp__{server}__{tool}. Subagent-inheritance + #27203 caveats apply identically. ARCHITECTURE_DRAFT §4.2 Law #1 names only Brain MCP proposals as Gateway intents; §6 brainclient handles Brain MCP, but no module governs agent-invoked third-party MCP tool mutations.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Harness Adapter Layer + §Action Gateway: extend the can_use_tool-coverage spike (OQ-HARN-SPIKE-7) to enumerate MCP tool interception explicitly; define policy for agent-invoked non-Brain MCP tools that mutate (deny by default, or require they route through the Gateway); document that any MCP server NexusOps allows into a supervised session is part of the trust boundary.

findings.finding: The libgit2 relative-worktrees claim in ADR-007/RESEARCH R-GIT (relied on to justify the dual-git split) is potentially STALE and its SCOPE is unverified — and the scope is load-bearing. (a) Currency: libgit2 issue #7210 (and PR #7254) now appear CLOSED/resolved per current GitHub state, whereas RESEARCH.md/ADR-007 assert the fix is 'in-flight / unreleased' (#7210/#7254). If shipped in the bundled libgit2, ADR-007's 'What Would Change This' trigger has fired. (b) Scope: the draft assumes git2 READS (status/diff/log) are always safe and only worktree MUTATIONS need the CLI. But libgit2 errors with 'unsupported extension name extensions.relativeworktrees' — historically this is raised at repository-open / extension-check time, which would break the git2 READ path entirely on any repo that has the extension set (git >=2.48 with worktree.useRelativePaths). Since agents and cc-crew create worktrees (Claude ships native --worktree), repos in NexusOps's own workflow are exactly the ones likely to carry this extension. RESEARCH did not verify whether reads survive; OQ-INT-SPIKE-6 covers a 're-check' but doesn't call out the read-path-breakage risk.
findings.evidence: WebSearch + GitHub: libgit2#7210 'libgit2 doesn't support relative worktrees (as per git >= 2.48)'; #7099 'error: unsupported extension name extensions.relativeworktree'; current state indicates #7210/#7254 closed (resolution likely merged); error historically surfaces on extension validation at repo open. RESEARCH.md L123 / ADR-007 L176: 'libgit2 can't do extensions.relativeworktrees (git >=2.48; errors outright; fix in-flight #7210/#7254)'; ADR-007 'What Would Change This' = 'libgit2 shipping relative-worktree support'.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Git Layer + OQ-INT-SPIKE-6: (1) Re-verify the libgit2 version bundled by the chosen git2-rs and whether #7210 is fixed there; update ADR-007's currency. (2) Sharpen the spike to test the READ path specifically: open + status + diff + log via git2 on a repo with extensions.relativeworktrees set; if reads fail, ADR-007's 'git2 for hot reads' assumption is invalid for these repos and the source-of-truth matrix (DATA_MODEL §3) must fall back to git-CLI reads for them. (3) Pin git2-rs/libgit2 versions in §Versioning.

findings.finding: The Codex app-server 'partly experimental' caveat (R-CODEX, ADR-006) is correct in spirit but imprecise about WHICH dependencies are experimental — and the architecture binds to several methods without stating their stability tier. Current docs show the methods NexusOps depends on for MVP — thread/start, thread/resume, thread/list, turn/start, thread/status/changed, and the host-routed approval flow item/commandExecution/requestApproval — are STABLE (no experimentalApi requirement), while experimentalApi gates only advanced features (thread/fork ephemeral, thread/turns/list, settings/memory/process/* methods, dynamic tools). This is GOOD NEWS the draft does not capture: it over-states the experimental risk for the core path while under-pinning the exact contract. Additionally, the approval flow has version-tiering the draft misses: modern item/commandExecution/requestApproval vs legacy execCommandApproval/applyPatchApproval for older app-server versions — the adapter must handle both or pin a min version. The WebSocket transport (separate from stdio) is explicitly experimental, and -32001 overload errors must be treated as transient retryable.
findings.evidence: github.com/openai/codex codex-rs/app-server/README + developers.openai.com/codex/app-server: experimentalApi gates thread/fork(ephemeral), thread/turns/list, thread/turns/items/list, thread/settings/update, thread/memoryMode/set, memory/reset, backgroundTerminals/clean, environment/add, process/*; thread/start, thread/resume, thread/list, turn/start, thread/status/changed are stable. item/commandExecution/requestApproval is the modern stable approval request (also carries MCP-tool-call approval elicitations codex_approval_kind:'mcp_tool_call'); legacy execCommandApproval/applyPatchApproval handled for older versions. Stability warnings: WebSocket transport experimental; pin version + regenerate schemas; treat -32001 overload as transient.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Harness Adapter Layer (Codex model) + §Versioning: (1) Enumerate the EXACT app-server methods the MVP adapter depends on and tag each stable/experimental; record that the core path is stable (downgrade TR-02's 'partly experimental' framing for the core path while keeping the schema-pin/CI-regen mitigation). (2) Specify the legacy-vs-modern approval handling (handle both, or declare a pinned minimum Codex version). (3) Add -32001 overload as a transient/retryable error class in the adapter contract. (4) Note that Codex's approval flow DOES cover MCP-tool-call elicitations — a coverage advantage over Claude's gap (finding 1/3) worth recording in the cross-harness comparison.

findings.finding: Agent-CLI version churn is acknowledged for telemetry/schema (TR-02/TR-03, OQ-HARN-9) but the architecture pins NO concrete versions and defines NO version-floor for the behaviors it depends on, despite the plan stating 'pin a tested version'. Both CLIs move weekly-to-monthly: Claude Code CLI ~v2.1.167 with `total_input_tokens` semantics ALREADY changed at v2.1.132; Codex CLI 0.137.0 (2026-06-04) with app-server method/shape drift between releases; the Agent SDK itself is ~0.3.x and the #27203 subagent bug is tied to a specific SDK version (~0.2.42). Without a named pinned tuple {Claude Code CLI, claude-agent-sdk, Codex CLI} in the binding contract, the adapter conformance suite (DRAFT §14) has nothing to pin against, and the 're-verify on bump' policy has no baseline. This is the difference between a testable contract and an untestable aspiration.
findings.evidence: RESEARCH.md L58 (CLI ~v2.1.167; SDK ~0.3.x; total_input_tokens changed at v2.1.132), L75 (Codex 0.137.0 2026-06-04); TR-02/TR-03 say 'version-pin' but name no version; OQ-HARN-8 'pin Codex version' / OQ-HARN-9 'pin Claude version' both OPEN; #27203 referenced at sdk 0.2.42; DRAFT §16 'Codex app-server schema bundle is version-pinned' with no number.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Versioning & Handshake: record a concrete pinned version tuple {Claude Code CLI, @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk / claude-agent-sdk, Codex CLI} validated by the spikes, plus a documented minimum-supported floor and the CI gate (golden-fixture + schema-diff) that fails on drift. Make the adapter conformance suite (DRAFT §14) run against exactly these pins. Bind to OQ-HARN-8/9 and the spike outcomes.

findings.finding: octocrab merge-PR / GitHub-App ergonomics (OQ-INT-SPIKE-6, ADR-007 'What Would Change This') is the lowest-risk of the named deps and is now largely de-risked: octocrab supports GitHub-App auth (OctocrabBuilder::app, installation(), installation_token()) and a pulls() PullRequestHandler. The merge() method on the PR handler was not visible in the fetched docs excerpt, so the specific merge call remains the one item warranting the spot-check the spike already owes. No architectural change needed; this is the correctly-scoped 'acceptable risk, spot-check' bucket — recording it so it is not conflated with the genuinely load-bearing deps above.
findings.evidence: docs.rs/octocrab Octocrab struct: pulls(owner,repo)->PullRequestHandler; OctocrabBuilder::app, installation(), installation_and_token(), installation_token(), installation_token_with_buffer() for GitHub-App installation auth. merge() on PullRequestHandler not shown in the fetched excerpt. ADR-007 fallback already provides shell `gh` for octocrab gaps.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Integration Architecture: keep OQ-INT-SPIKE-6 as a low-stakes pre-build spot-check (confirm pulls().merge() signature + a real App-installation token flow); document the shell-`gh` fallback as already specified. No structural change.

findings.finding: Cross-harness mutation-coverage ASYMMETRY is unaccounted for in the one-contract abstraction (ADR-006, DRAFT §9.1). The research now shows the two harnesses have DIFFERENT mutation-interception coverage: Codex's host-routed approval (item/commandExecution/requestApproval) covers command execution, patch application, AND MCP-tool-call elicitations (codex_approval_kind:'mcp_tool_call'), giving broad coverage; Claude's can_use_tool has the subagent/background-bash/permission-mode holes in finding 1. The HarnessAdapter contract `{launch, stream-status, intercept-mutation, ...}` assumes 'intercept-mutation' is uniformly reliable across both, but it is materially weaker on Claude. A single conformance suite that passes on Codex could give false confidence about Claude. The 'agent-agnostic Gateway' premise is sound only if the adapter contract surfaces each harness's interception GAPS as first-class, not hidden behind a uniform method.
findings.evidence: Finding 1 (Claude subagent/mode holes, #27203) vs Codex approval covering command+patch+mcp_tool_call elicitations (codex app-server README / developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security). ADR-006 L151 treats intercept-mutation as one uniform contract method; DRAFT §14 specifies 'a shared HarnessAdapter conformance suite run against both' without per-harness coverage assertions.
findings.proposed_fix: ARCHITECTURE.md §Harness Adapter Layer: add a per-harness 'mutation-coverage matrix' to the contract documenting, per tool category (direct-bash/file-edit/subagent/background/MCP), whether interception is guaranteed, best-effort, or unsupported — so the Gateway can apply compensating controls (e.g. deny-rules, forbidding background subagents on Claude) where interception is weak. The §14 conformance suite must assert coverage per category per harness, not a single shared pass.
